entities.name: Emperor Zhao of Han
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Emperor Zhao of Han was the eighth emperor of the Han dynasty, reigning from 87 to 74 BC. Born Liu Fuling (劉弗陵), he was the youngest son of Emperor Wu and succeeded his brother Xuan. Zhao's reign was marked by internal conflicts and external pressures, including the rise of the Xiongnu nomads to the north.

The most notable event during his reign was the failed invasion of the Xiongnu, which ended in defeat and a devastating war. The Han dynasty suffered greatly due to this defeat, leading to significant changes in the country's military strategy and alliances with neighboring states.

Despite these challenges, Emperor Zhao implemented several policies aimed at strengthening the economy and improving infrastructure. He also promoted trade and commerce, both domestically and internationally.

In his later years, Emperor Zhao faced increasing opposition from within his own court, ultimately leading to his downfall. His reign came to an end with his death in 73 BC, marking a significant turning point for the Han dynasty.

"The wise man can learn more from his enemies than his friends." - Emperor Zhao of Han
